headline: Q3 organic growth slowed to 1% as China weighed; Fashion & Leather Goods -5% while US, Europe and Japan grew.
key_messages: Fashion & Leather Goods -5% organic (vs ~-1.8% expected): strong US demand offset by weaker China; LV hurt by China backlash.
Wines & Spirits +6% organic; Selective Retailing +8% led by Sephora market-share gains.
Group organic +1% (9M +2%); US about +5% in Q3 and +4% in 9M; China less buoyant.

consumer.big_ticket: US luxury demand good, especially fashion and leather goods; China the main drag.

macro_read: Wealthy US consumers were among luxury's steadier buyers in Q3 2026 while China faltered, so US high-end spending is holding up better than global luxury.
notes: The U.S. figure comes from one secondary summary of LVMH's results slides.
LVMH is listed in Paris and reports in euros. It does not file with the SEC, so this card is refreshed on request, not automatically.
Released after Paris close; shares fell more than 1% on 2026-10-13 (one report -1.83% early), exact close not confirmed so no stock move is shown.
US +5% comes from a single secondary source (Investing.com summary of LVMH slides); LVMH's release text says only 'good growth'.
Reported Q3 YoY revenue change not confirmed; 9M reported revenue -2% to EUR 57.148B.
